title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 483-485): Grothendieck is analysing a profinite object M̃_{0,3}, the set or group of 'rigidified' solutions of the loop equation for the (0,3) Teichmüller stratum. An element can be given by a triple (α,β,γ), and the analysis goes through its linear shadow in SL(2,Ẑ) or GL(2,Ẑ), i.e. what is seen on the abelianisation of the free profinite group π. On the previous page each element of the subobject M̃_{0,3}[0] yields an affine matrix u = [[1/D, B/D],[0,1]]. Here (A B; C D) is the image of ξ = αγ(α)^{-1}, subject to ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ) = ±1 with ρ of order 3. In terms of α = (a b; c d) one has ε'D = c²+cd+d² and ε'B = ac+bd+bc. The normalised part M̃_{0,3}(0) is cut out by B = 0, i.e. u lies in the Borel Γ_0(Ẑ).

This page:
(1) The normalisation gives canonical semidirect ('1/2-direct') decompositions:
- (44) M̃_{0,3}[0] ≃ M̃_{0,3}(0) · L_0π, with L_0π a group attached to π that acts as a translation/inner part;
- (45) M̃_{0,3} ≃ M̃_{0,3}(0) · 𝔖^{+∧}_{0,3}, with 𝔖^{+∧}_{0,3} the (completed, oriented) symmetry group of the three marked points.
So every element factors uniquely as a normalised element times a 'symmetry' element.
(2) To describe the homomorphism (34), Θ^π_G (an action of M̃_{0,3} on G/π), it suffices to know it on the two factors. On 𝔖^{+∧} it is already known. One must then describe it on M̃_{0,3}[0], or even only on M̃_{0,3}(0), modulo a series of compatibility checks.
- (46) On M̃_{0,3}[0], Θ^π_G coincides with the previously constructed (33), Θ^π_{B'_0}.
- (47) On the normalised part M̃_{0,3}(0), Θ^π_G(u) = i_{T_0}(μ), where μ is the 'multiplication' (the diagonal unit 1/D ∈ Ẑ^*) of u. This is the image of a torus element, so the action is essentially trivial: it is just scalar/cyclotomic-type multiplication.
Grothendieck notes that (47) can even serve as a definition of M̃_{0,3}(0).
(3) Remark (continued on the next page): since Θ^π_G was built 'à la force des poignets' through Θ^π_{B'_0}, i.e. U was built from u, he long confused u and U. The confusion was dissipated only 'hier et aujourd'hui'.

Structurally, this is the same pattern as the later normalisation of Grothendieck–Teichmüller elements (λ,f). There, normalised elements act on generators by a pure power x ↦ x^λ up to conjugation, the 3-cycle relation f(x,y)f(y,z)f(z,x) = 1 mirrors ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ) = ±1, and the residual symmetry is the S_3 or Z/3 of the three points.
errors: No mathematical error detectable on this page; the claims are stated without proof ('moyennant une série de compatibilités'). The exact nature of L_0π and 𝔖^{+∧}_{0,3}, and whether the products are left or right semidirect, cannot be checked from this page alone.
Equation label: the transcription's '(36)' (equivalently the image's '(3̶6)') must be (46), since the sequence on the page is 44, 45, 46, 47.

ideas.what: Canonical semidirect decomposition of the (0,3) object into a normalised part (B=0, u in Borel Γ_0(Ẑ)) times a symmetry group of the three points, resp. times L_0π
ideas.modern_name: Normalisation of GT-type elements / splitting off the S_3 (or Z/3) symmetry and inner automorphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990) and Ihara (1990s) for the normalisation in GT
ideas.where_published: Possibly sketched in La Longue Marche (1981); not in this form in Esquisse

ideas.what: On normalised elements the action Θ^π_G reduces to a torus element given by the multiplier μ (diagonal unit)
ideas.modern_name: Action of normalised (λ,f) on generators by x ↦ x^λ (cyclotomic-character part)

ideas.what: Reduction of the description of a homomorphism on a semidirect product to its factors, up to compatibilities

missed.claim: This is an early, independent instance of the 'normalised element + symmetry' factorisation for profinite genus-0 Teichmüller data, worked out through the SL(2,Ẑ) shadow (quadratic form c²+cd+d², 3-cycle relation). It is mainly of historical interest as a precursor of GT normalisation; no new theorem is evident.
missed.quote: obtenir des décompositions canoniques en produits ½-directs (44) M̃_{0,3}[0] ≃ M̃_{0,3}(0).L_0π (45) M̃_{0,3} ≃ M̃_{0,3}(0).𝔖^{+∧}_{0,3}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck had the normalisation/splitting structure for the (0,3) level before Drinfeld–Ihara. This is relevant to the history of GT, but not mathematically new.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an internal step of a long computation: semidirect decompositions and the observation that normalised elements act by a scalar. The ideas are now standard in GT theory. There is mild historical interest as a possible anticipation of the normalisation conventions.
